lead: Hierarchical clustering builds a tree of nested clusters. It is used when the number of clusters is not known in advance. The tree, called a dendrogram, shows how points merge or split at different distance levels. It helps in market segmentation, gene expression analysis, and grouping similar cities for logistics planning.
prereq: You need: basic distance concepts from Unsupervised learning and types of clustering and matrix handling from K-means clustering algorithm.

blocks.text: Linkage defines the distance between two clusters. Single linkage uses the smallest pairwise distance. Complete linkage uses the largest pairwise distance. Average linkage uses the mean of all pairwise distances.

blocks.where: d_single is the single‑linkage distance; C_i and C_j are clusters; distance(x,y) is the chosen metric, e.g., Euclidean.
d_average is the average‑linkage distance; |C_i| is the number of points in C_i; |C_j| is the number of points in C_j.

blocks.text: Single linkage tends to produce long, chain‑like clusters. Complete linkage gives compact, spherical clusters. Average linkage balances the two.

items: Start with each point as a separate cluster.
Compute the distance matrix between all clusters.
Find the pair with the smallest linkage distance.
Merge the pair into a new cluster.
Update the distance matrix using the chosen linkage rule.
Repeat until only one cluster remains.

blocks.text: The distance matrix is symmetric. After a merge, only the row and column of the new cluster need to be recomputed.

items: Matrix size reduces by one after each merge.
The algorithm runs in O(n³) time for naive implementation.
Efficient implementations can achieve O(n²) time, for example using the Lance‑Williams update with a priority queue.

sections.h3: Dendrogram interpretation and brief note on divisive clustering

blocks.text: A dendrogram plots the merge distance on the vertical axis. Cutting the tree at a height h yields all clusters whose merge distance is ≤ h.
Divisive clustering starts with all points in one cluster and splits recursively. It is less common because it requires a good splitting criterion.
In practice, agglomerative clustering is used for customer segmentation, image segmentation, and arranging railway stations by travel time.

examples.question: Four cities A, B, C, D have road distances (km): A‑B = 10, A‑C = 20, A‑D = 30, B‑C = 15, B‑D = 25, C‑D = 12. Using agglomerative single‑linkage clustering, list the merges and the distance at which each merge occurs.
steps: Initial clusters: {A}, {B}, {C}, {D}. Distance matrix shows smallest distance 10 (A‑B).
Merge A and B into cluster AB at distance 10.
Update distances: d(AB, C)=min(20,15)=15; d(AB, D)=min(30,25)=25; d(C, D)=12.
Smallest remaining distance is 12 (C‑D). Merge C and D into cluster CD at distance 12.
Update distance between AB and CD: min(15,25)=15.
Only two clusters remain. Merge AB and CD at distance 15.
examples.answer: Merges are (A,B) at 10 km, (C,D) at 12 km, and (AB,CD) at 15 km.

code.code:
import sys
# Simple single‑linkage agglomerative clustering for four points
points = ['A','B','C','D']
# distance matrix as dict of tuple -> value
D = {('A','B'):10,('A','C'):20,('A','D'):30,('B','C'):15,('B','D'):25,('C','D'):12}
clusters = [{p} for p in points]
merges = []
while len(clusters) > 1:
    # find closest pair of clusters
    min_dist = float('inf')
    pair = None
    for i in range(len(clusters)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(clusters)):
            # single linkage distance = min over all pairs
            d = min(D.get(tuple(sorted((x,y))) ) for x in clusters[i] for y in clusters[j])
            if d < min_dist:
                min_dist = d
                pair = (i,j)
    i,j = pair
    new_cluster = clusters[i] | clusters[j]
    merges.append((clusters[i], clusters[j], min_dist))
    # remove old clusters and add new
    clusters = [c for k,c in enumerate(clusters) if k not in (i,j)]
    clusters.append(new_cluster)
for a,b,dist in merges:
    print('Merge',a,'and',b,'at',dist)

traps: Using the complete‑linkage formula when the question asks for single‑linkage gives a larger merge distance.
Forgetting to recompute distances after a merge leads to wrong subsequent merges.
Treating the distance matrix as directed; the matrix is symmetric, so (A,B) and (B,A) are the same.
Assuming the number of clusters is fixed; hierarchical clustering continues until one cluster remains.

quiz.q: What is the name of the tree that visualises hierarchical clustering?
Explain why single linkage can produce chain‑like clusters.
quiz.a: Single linkage always picks the smallest pairwise distance. It can keep adding points that are only slightly close to the existing cluster, stretching the cluster into a chain.

quiz.q: Given points X, Y, Z with pairwise distances 5, 9, and 12, perform one step of agglomerative single‑linkage clustering.
quiz.a: The smallest distance is 5 between X and Y. Merge X and Y into a new cluster XY. The distance from XY to Z is min(9,12)=9.

quiz.q: In the example of four cities, what distance is used to merge the final two clusters?
Compare the effect of using average linkage versus complete linkage on a dataset with outliers.
quiz.a: Average linkage reduces the influence of outliers by averaging all pairwise distances, so a single extreme distance has less impact than in complete linkage.

quiz.q: Name the three common linkage criteria.
quiz.a: Single linkage, complete linkage, average linkage.

quiz.q: Why does a dendrogram allow the analyst to choose the number of clusters after clustering is complete?
quiz.a: Because cutting the dendrogram at a chosen height groups all merges below that height into clusters. Different heights produce different numbers of clusters.

beyond: Not for the exam. Hierarchical clustering is used in bioinformatics to build phylogenetic trees. Cloud providers use it to group similar usage patterns for auto‑scaling. Recent research explores hybrid methods that combine hierarchical and density‑based clustering. Search for "scalable agglomerative clustering" and "dendrogram visualization" for further reading.
